orientation.heading: Orientation
orientation.rule: Every boundary faces away from what it bounds. This is GeoJSON's right-hand rule, carried to every dimension:
orientation.polygon: A polygon's exterior ring runs counterclockwise, and its holes run clockwise.
orientation.polyhedron: A polyhedron's faces, by the right-hand rule, turn their normals away from the solid, and so into any void inside it.
orientation.polychoron: A polychoron's cells face away from it in the same way.
orientation.neighbours: So the two neighbours of every shared boundary traverse it in opposite directions: each edge of a polyhedron by two faces, each face of a polychoron by two cells. A point's winding number is then 1 inside the solid, and 0 outside it or in a void.
orientation.void: A void needs no nesting level of its own: it is a boundary that faces the other way. The types check only the nesting depth, so a twisted or open boundary still type-checks, just as an open ring does in GeoJSON.

check.no-coordinates: Nothing here has coordinates to draw.
check.not-a-position: A position must be a list of numbers.
check.ragged: These items are nested to different depths.
check.type-depth: {type} nests positions {expected} levels deep, but this nests them {found}.
check.mixed-dimension: Positions have different numbers of coordinates; shorter ones are padded with zeros to {dimension}.
check.open-ring: This ring does not end where it starts.
check.short-ring: A ring needs at least 4 positions, counting the closing one.
check.twisted: Some boundaries face inward and some outward, so the boundary is twisted (see the orientation rule).
check.inside-out: Every boundary faces inward: the solid is inside out.
check.hole-direction: This hole runs the same way as the outer ring; in GeoJSON, holes run clockwise.
